title: Intelligent-Tiering: automatic tiering without retrieval fees
must_teach: Moves objects Frequent -> Infrequent (30 days unaccessed) -> Archive Instant (90 days) automatically, with optional opt-in Archive (90+) and Deep Archive (180+) tiers; charges $0.0025 per 1,000 objects monitored, no retrieval fees, no minimum duration; objects <128 KB stay in Frequent at Frequent price. Use for unknown or changing access; not for tiny objects.

title: When storage scales itself and when you must size it
must_teach: S3 and EFS have no size to plan; RDS Storage Autoscaling grows storage when free space <10% for 5 min up to a max threshold (no shrink); EBS Elastic Volumes grow online but never shrink and gp3 IOPS/throughput scale independently; DynamoDB storage is unlimited. Rule: enable RDS autoscaling with a ceiling instead of over-provisioning; snapshot-and-recreate to shrink.

unit: Determining the required availability for different classes of workloads
title: Dev/test environment used 09:00-18:00 weekdays: cheapest design
must_teach: Single-AZ, On-Demand or Spot, stopped outside hours by a scheduler (Instance Scheduler/EventBridge), RDS stopped or Aurora Serverless v2; production keeps Multi-AZ with commitments.
distractor_angles: Multi-AZ with RIs for dev violates least-cost (paying for availability not needed); 3-year RIs for a 45-hour week violate utilization; leaving it running violates least-cost; Spot for the production tier violates the availability class.

must_teach: Compute Savings Plan (or RIs) for the steady tier and Spot Instances (or Fargate Spot) for the batch; the two plausible sets differ on whether Spot is allowed for the web tier.
distractor_angles: Spot for the web tier violates availability constraint; On-Demand for the batch violates least-cost; Dedicated Hosts wrong feature (licensing); 3-year EC2 Instance SP on the batch violates flexibility (batch could move families).

title: Low-traffic Linux web servers with rare bursts: cheapest family
must_teach: T4g (Graviton burstable) in standard mode; sustained load would need M7g; unlimited mode can surcharge.

unit: Selecting the appropriate instance size for a workload
title: Fleet averages 8% CPU before a 3-year commitment

unit: Determining an appropriate load balancing strategy (ALB vs NLB vs GWLB)
title: Twelve HTTP microservices, one domain, fewest load balancers
must_teach: One ALB with host/path-based routing to twelve target groups; NLB cannot route by path and GWLB is for appliances.

unit: Determining appropriate scaling methods and strategies (horizontal vs vertical, hibernation)
title: Long in-memory warm-up, idle nights, must resume in seconds
must_teach: Hibernate at night (no instance charge, RAM preserved) rather than stopping (loses RAM) or keeping running; horizontal scaling does not fix per-instance warm-up.
distractor_angles: Stop/start violates the fast-resume constraint (RAM lost); keep running violates least-cost; warm pool in Running state violates least-cost; vertical scale-down still bills hours and does not preserve state.

unit: Determining appropriate scaling methods and strategies for elastic workloads
title: Load spikes every weekday 09:00 with slow instance boot
must_teach: Predictive scaling (or scheduled scaling when the pattern is fixed) launches capacity before the spike so the group can run leaner otherwise; target tracking alone reacts too late.
distractor_angles: Target tracking only violates the boot-time constraint; running peak capacity 24x7 violates least-cost; vertical scaling violates elasticity; step scaling on CPU is superseded by predictive for a known daily pattern.

unit: Optimization of compute utilization (containers, serverless, microservices)
title: Raising utilization: containers, serverless, and when each is cheapest
must_teach: Cost follows idle capacity. Containers on EC2 bin-pack many services on fewer hosts (cheapest at steady high utilization, you patch hosts); Fargate charges per task-second with no idle host (cheapest for spiky or small services); Lambda charges per request + GB-s (cheapest when invocations are sporadic and short, <15 min). Break-even rule of thumb: sustained >~60-70% utilization favours EC2/ECS-on-EC2 with a Savings Plan; bursty favours Fargate/Lambda.

title: Tags and multi-account billing for compute: RI and SP sharing
must_teach: In an organization, RI and Savings Plans discounts are shared across all member accounts by default (payer can turn sharing off per account), which is why buying commitments centrally in the management account covers everyone. Cost allocation tags on EC2/ASG/Lambda let Cost Explorer show utilization per team; AWS-generated aws:createdBy tags help attribute untagged spend. Trap: sharing applies within one organization and one Region for zonal RIs.

title: Cost tools for compute: RI/SP recommendations and rightsizing
must_teach: Cost Explorer hosts Savings Plans/RI purchase recommendations (based on 7/30/60 days of On-Demand usage) and EC2 rightsizing recommendations; Budgets supports RI/SP utilization and coverage budgets (alert when a commitment sits under 80% used); Compute Optimizer gives per-instance family/size recommendations; CUR amortizes upfront RI/SP cost per hour for showback. Trusted Advisor cost checks (idle instances, low utilization) need Business/Enterprise support.

title: Edge processing as a cost lever
must_teach: Move small, request-shaped logic to the edge so origin compute and transfer shrink: CloudFront Functions (sub-ms, $0.10/M, header rewrites/redirects), Lambda@Edge (heavier logic, per-request + GB-s), and Snowball Edge / Outposts for processing where data is created so only results cross the WAN. Rule: if the work needs no origin data and runs per request, edge is cheaper than a fleet behind a load balancer; if it needs the database, it is not.

title: Regions and AZs as cost variables

Spot prices and capacity vary per AZ and instance pool, so diversifying AZs lowers Spot interruption and cost. Local Zones/Wavelength/Outposts cost more than the parent Region.

title: Instance family letters, generations and sizes as a cost decision
must_teach: Family letter = resource ratio (C compute, R/X memory, M balanced, T burstable, I/D storage, G/P accelerated); the newest generation is usually cheaper per unit of performance; size doubles vCPU/RAM and price linearly, so two smaller instances cost the same as one larger and add resilience. Cost traps: paying for an R when the app is CPU-bound, running T instances in unlimited mode under sustained load (surcharge), and choosing an older generation because the AMI is old.

unit: AWS purchasing options (Spot, Reserved, Savings Plans)
title: On-Demand vs Reserved vs Savings Plans vs Spot decision rule
must_teach: Steady 24x7 baseline -> Savings Plans (flexible) or RIs (capacity reservation when zonal); interruptible/stateless -> Spot (up to 90% off, 2-minute notice); unpredictable or short-lived -> On-Demand; licence-bound -> Dedicated Hosts. Mix them: commit for the floor, Spot for burst, On-Demand for the rest. The trap options are Spot for a database or a single stateful server, and a 3-year RI for a workload that may change family or Region.

Cache hit ratio is the metric; a cache in front of a write-heavy DB saves nothing.

unit: VPC peering vs Transit Gateway pricing
title: When peering is the cheaper topology
must_teach: Peering: no hourly fee, same-AZ data free, cross-AZ $0.01/GB each way, inter-Region peering at inter-Region rates. TGW: ~$0.05/attachment-hour (~$36/month per VPC) + $0.02/GB. Few VPCs with heavy same-AZ traffic -> peering; many VPCs, hybrid, shared services or inspection -> TGW; TGW also enables one central NAT/egress VPC.

unit: Bandwidth allocation: single vs multiple VPNs, Direct Connect speed
title: 1.25 Gbps per tunnel; ECMP over TGW; DX speed ladder
must_teach: A Site-to-Site VPN tunnel caps at 1.25 Gbps; a virtual private gateway cannot aggregate, but Transit Gateway with ECMP spreads flows across multiple VPN connections (each ~$36/month) to multiply bandwidth cheaply. Beyond a few Gbps or for consistent latency use DX: hosted 50 Mbps-25 Gbps (cheapest entry), dedicated 1/10/100/400 Gbps, LAG to bundle ports. Trap: buying a 10 Gbps DX for 500 Mbps of bursty traffic.

title: MGN: lift-and-shift servers to EC2
must_teach: MGN replicates on-prem/other-cloud servers block-level into a low-cost staging area (t3.small replication servers + EBS) and launches cutover instances with minutes of downtime; the service itself is free for 90 days per server, you pay staging resources. Use for rehost at scale. Not for databases with engine change (DMS/SCT), not for file data (DataSync), not for refactoring.

title: Aurora Serverless v2: pay per ACU-second
must_teach: Aurora Serverless v2 scales an Aurora instance between min and max ACUs (0.5 ACU steps, can now pause to 0) in seconds and bills per ACU-second, so it is cheapest for dev/test, spiky, or multi-tenant workloads; it can be mixed with provisioned instances in one cluster. Not cheaper for a steady 24x7 load (provisioned + reserved wins) and v1 is deprecated. Trap: a min ACU set too low evicts the buffer pool.

title: AWS Budgets: what it is, when to use it, when not
must_teach: Budgets sets thresholds on cost, usage, RI/SP utilization or coverage and alerts (email/SNS/Chatbot) on actual or forecasted values; budget actions can apply an IAM/SCP policy or stop EC2/RDS. Data refreshes up to 3x/day, so it cannot stop a runaway in minutes. Not for analysis (Cost Explorer) or line items (CUR); first two action-enabled budgets free, then $0.10/day each.

title: DataSync: managed bulk transfer and sync
must_teach: Agent-based (or agentless between AWS services) transfer at ~$0.0125/GB with scheduling, bandwidth throttling, filters, checksums, and direct writes into any S3 class, EFS or FSx. Use for one-time migrations and recurring syncs over internet/VPN/DX. Not for partner-facing protocols (Transfer Family), not for continuous on-prem cache access (Storage Gateway), not when the link makes it slower than shipping a Snowball.

title: DMS: database migration with minimal downtime
must_teach: DMS runs a replication instance (or DMS Serverless) that does full load plus change data capture between many engines, on-prem to AWS or AWS to AWS; SCT (free) converts schemas for heterogeneous moves. Billed per replication-instance hour plus storage; DMS Free offers 6 months free when migrating to Aurora/Redshift/DynamoDB/DocumentDB. Not for server migration (MGN) or file data (DataSync).

title: EBS: block storage for one instance
must_teach: Network block volumes (gp3 default) attached to one instance in one AZ (io2 Multi-Attach excepted), billed per provisioned GB and IOPS/throughput whether used or not, snapshotted incrementally to S3. Use for boot volumes, databases, anything needing random block I/O. Not for shared access across instances (EFS/FSx), object data (S3), or scratch data where instance store is free.

title: EC2: when a VM is the right (and cheapest) choice
must_teach: EC2 is the general-purpose VM billed per second (Linux, 60 s minimum) by instance type; choose it when you need OS control, long-running steady load (with Savings Plans), GPUs, licences (Dedicated Hosts) or lift-and-shift. When not: sporadic short tasks (Lambda), containers without host management (Fargate), managed database/queue/file services that replace self-hosting. Cost levers in order: rightsize, Graviton, purchasing option, schedule/stop, Spot.

title: FSx flavours and their cost levers
must_teach: FSx for Windows (SMB, AD, SSD or cheaper HDD, dedup), FSx for Lustre (HPC/ML, scratch is cheaper than persistent, S3-linked), FSx for NetApp ONTAP (multi-protocol, capacity-pool tier for cold data, compression), FSx for OpenZFS. Billed per provisioned GB and throughput. Use when a specific file protocol or feature is required; not when EFS (Linux NFS, pay-per-use) or S3 suffices.

title: Outposts: AWS hardware in your data centre
must_teach: Outposts racks/servers run EC2, EBS, ECS/EKS, RDS, S3 on Outposts locally as an extension of a Region AZ, managed by AWS, ordered on a 3-year term. Use for data residency, sub-ms latency to on-prem equipment, or local processing with occasional connectivity. Not for cost saving or disconnected sites (needs a link to the parent Region; Snowball Edge for offline).

title: S3 Glacier classes: cold storage economics
must_teach: Three classes: Glacier Instant Retrieval (ms access, 90-day min, quarterly access), Glacier Flexible Retrieval (expedited 1-5 min, standard 3-5 h, bulk 5-12 h free; 90-day min), Deep Archive (12 h standard, 48 h bulk, 180-day min, cheapest ~$1/TB-month). Retrieval fees plus 40 KB metadata overhead per object make millions of tiny objects expensive. Not for data needed within seconds unless Instant Retrieval.

title: S3: when object storage is right and when it is not
must_teach: S3 stores unlimited whole objects with 11 nines durability, billed per GB by class plus requests and egress; it is the cheapest durable store and the default for static content, backups, logs, data lakes. Not for block/boot volumes, POSIX file semantics, in-place partial writes, or sub-ms transactional access. Cost levers: storage class, lifecycle, request batching, CloudFront for egress, endpoints for in-VPC access.

title: Savings Plans: flexible commitment discounts
must_teach: Commit $/hour for 1 or 3 years: Compute SP (up to 66%, any Region/family/OS, EC2 + Fargate + Lambda), EC2 Instance SP (up to 72%, one family in one Region), SageMaker SP. Applied automatically to matching usage after RIs. When not: you need a capacity reservation (zonal RI or ODCR), the workload is Spot-suitable, or spend is unpredictable below the commitment (unused commitment is still billed).
gap_note: Good; note SPs never reserve capacity.

title: Snow Family: offline transfer and edge compute
must_teach: Snowcone (8/14 TB, portable), Snowball Edge Storage Optimized (up to 210 TB) and Compute Optimized (GPU/compute at the edge); priced per job plus daily fees after the included days, with free data ingress into S3. Use when transfer time over the network exceeds ~a week or connectivity is poor; Snowmobile is discontinued. Not for ongoing sync (DataSync) or small datasets.

title: Storage Gateway: hybrid access to S3-backed storage
must_teach: S3 File Gateway (NFS/SMB shares as objects), Volume Gateway (iSCSI cached or stored, backed by EBS snapshots), Tape Gateway (VTL to S3/Glacier); billed per GB written plus storage, hardware appliance optional. Use for continued on-prem access with cloud-backed capacity or to retire tape. Not for one-off migration (DataSync) or partner SFTP (Transfer Family).

must_teach: A fully managed protocol endpoint (identity via service-managed, AD, or custom Lambda IdP) that lands files in S3 or EFS; billed ~$0.30/hour per enabled protocol plus $0.04/GB, so ~$216/month idle. Use when external partners must keep their SFTP clients. Not for one-time internal migration (DataSync), not for high-volume bulk moves (Snow/DataSync).
